claims.text: The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are smaller than 5 nm.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have an FCC structure and near-equimolar composition.
In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, the surface-energy term in the Gibbs free energy dominates configurational-entropy stabilization.
The FCC phase in PLD-grown AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles is governed primarily by kinetic trapping rather than entropy stabilization.
Bulk HEAs exhibit sluggish diffusion because of lattice distortion and high mixing enthalpy.
Surface atoms in these nanoparticles have reduced coordination and a local chemical environment different from that of bulk atoms.
Reduced surface coordination makes the activation barrier for Au and Cu surface diffusion substantially lower than the corresponding bulk-diffusion barrier.
Au and Cu are the lowest-surface-energy constituents of the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Au and Cu segregate to the nanoparticle surface to reduce total surface energy.
The Au/Cu-enriched surface produces a chemical-potential or surface-energy gradient that drives rapid surface diffusion.
Surface-segregated Au and Cu evaporate at elevated temperatures because of their high vapor pressure, at temperatures well below the bulk solidus.
Preferential Au/Cu evaporation causes particle shrinkage.
Surface diffusion causes initially elliptical or icosahedral nanoparticles to become spherical by reducing surface area and homogenizing curvature.
Significant Au/Cu segregation and particle-size reduction begin at approximately 450–500 K.
The particle-size distribution widens because smaller particles evaporate completely before larger particles.
After Au/Cu depletion, the remaining particle core becomes enriched in Pt and Ni.
The surface-gradient mechanism dominates for AuCoCuNiPt particles smaller than 10 nm.
For particles larger than 20 nm, bulk sluggish diffusion dominates and preserves the FCC structure to higher temperatures.
Icosahedral nanoparticles reshape faster than truncated-octahedral nanoparticles because their surface energy is higher.
If sluggish diffusion controls the behavior, there should be no significant segregation or size change below 600 K and diffusion barriers should remain high at both surface and core sites.
